title: Neural circuit-specific gene manipulation in mouse brain in vivo using split-intein-mediated split-Cre system
protocol: Incubate 500 ng of the synthesized specific promoter DNA fragment with 1 μL Mlu1 and 1 μL Kpn1 in 1× reaction buffer at 37°C for 1 h.
Isolate the specific promoter DNA fragments by agarose gel electrophoresis using a gel extraction kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Cut each 500 ng of pAAV-Ef1α-CreN-InteinN and pAAV-Ef1α-InteinC-CreC plasmid with 1 μL Mlu1 and 1 μL Kpn1 in 1× reaction buffer at 37°C for 1 h.

Isolate and purify the 4,556 bp fragment from pAAV-Ef1α-CreN-InteinN and the 5,022 bp fragment from pAAV-Ef1α-InteinC-CreC plasmids using a gel extraction kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Discard the 1,275 bp fragment originating from the Ef1α promoter of each plasmid.
Insert the synthesized/cut promoter DNA fragment into the cut/linearized pAAV-CreN-InteinN or pAAV-InteinC-CreC vector using T4 DNA ligase according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Transform the ligated plasmids into Stbl3™ E. coli strain.
Spread the transformed Stbl3™ E. coli onto an LB agar plate containing 100 μg/mL carbenicillin.
Incubate the plate at 37°C overnight (16–24 h).
Inoculate a single colony into 5 mL of LB broth containing 100 μg/mL carbenicillin.
Incubate the LB broth at 37°C overnight (16–24 h) with shaking.
Centrifuge the 5 mL of Stbl3™ E. coli at 5,000 × g for 5 min at RT (20°C–22°C).
Extract and purify the plasmids using PureLink™ Quick Plasmid Miniprep Kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Identify pAAV-CreN-InteinN and pAAV-InteinC-CreC plasmids containing a specific promoter with Mlu1 and Kpn1 restriction enzyme.
Perform gel electrophoresis.
Prepare high-concentrated pAAV-CreN-InteinN and pAAV-InteinC-CreC plasmids using Plasmid Filter Maxiprep Kit according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Transfect the prepared plasmids into HEK293T cells for AAV production.
Purify the produced AAVs by iodixanol gradient ultracentrifugation.
Determine the titration of purified AAVs.
Maintain HEK293T cells in a 150 mm cell culture dish with DMEM/F-12 supplemented with 10% FBS and 1× penicillin-streptomycin at 37°C in a 5% CO2 humidified incubator.
Aspirate the media when HEK293T cells reach around 80% confluence, wash cells once with 20 ml of PBS to remove residual media.
Detach the cells with 2 ml of Trypsin-EDTA for 2 min at 37°C.
Neutralize trypsin activity by adding 10 ml of pre-warmed HEK293T cell culture media and suspend cells by gentle pipetting.
Transfer suspended HEK293T cells to a 50 ml tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 300 × g for 3 min at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet with 29 mL of pre-warmed HEK293T cell culture media.
Add the suspended HEK293T cells dropwise into six 150 mm cell culture dishes containing 15 mL of HEK293T cell culture media.
Gently shake the plates to spread the cells evenly on the plate surface.
Prepare three plasmids required for packaging AAVs.
Use pAAV-Ef1α-CreN-InteinN and pAAV-Ef1α-InteinC-CreC as AAV expression plasmids.
Use AAV2/8 (AAV8) and AAV-retro helper plasmids specific to the serotype.
Prepare the pAd-deltaF6 plasmid, an AAV helper plasmid carrying genes required for AAV replication.
Seed HEK293T cells twenty-four hours before transfection in six 150 mm cell culture dishes.

Mix 90 μg of pAD-deltaF6 plasmid, 45 μg of AAV-specific serotype plasmid (AAV2/8 or AAV-retro helper plasmid), and 45 μg of AAV expression plasmid (pAAV-Ef1α-CreN-InteinN or pAAV-Ef1α-InteinC-CreC) in Opti-MEM to make a total volume of 6 ml.
Mix 1 mL of 0.6 mg/mL PEI solution with 5 mL of Opti-MEM and vortex briefly.
Incubate the two mixtures separately at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for 10 minutes.
Combine the two previously prepared mixtures and vortex briefly.
Incubate the final mixture at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for 20 minutes.
Incubate the transfection mixture with HEK293T cells in a cell culture dish.
Aspirate the media after 6–12 hours of incubation.
Add pre-warmed fresh HEK293T cell culture media to the cell culture dishes.
Scrape transfected HEK293T cells off the 150 mm cell culture dish using a cell lifter.
Transfer cells and media from two dishes into a 50 mL tube.
Rinse the cell culture dish with PBS and transfer it to the same 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge the contents of the tube at 450 × g for 5 minutes at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Discard the supernatant by aspiration with a pasture pipette.
Repeat the collection step two more times to collect cells from six dishes.
Resuspend the transfected cell pellet with 4 mL of cell lysis buffer.
Freeze the pellet in a dry ice/ethanol mixture bath for 10 minutes.
Thaw the frozen pellet in a 37°C water bath for 10 minutes.
Shake the cell suspension thoroughly to lyse the cells and release AAV particles.
Repeat the freeze-thaw cycles four times.
Add Benzonase to achieve a final concentration of 50 U/mL.
Vortex briefly after adding Benzonase.
Incubate the tube in a 37°C water bath for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge at 3,500 × g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer supernatant containing AAV particles to a new 15 mL tube.
Prepare two 32 mL Beckman OptiSeal ultracentrifuge tubes for purification.
Add 5 mL of 60% iodixanol solution to the bottom of each tube using a 10 mL syringe with a 19-gauge needle.
Overlay 5 mL of 40% iodixanol solution on top of the 60% layer.
Gently load 6 mL of 25% iodixanol solution over the gradient.
Gently load 9 mL of 15% iodixanol solution over the gradient.
Add 5 mL of supernatant containing AAV particles to the top layer of the gradient tube by dripping slowly along the wall.
Fill up the iodixanol gradient tube with cell lysis buffer until reaching the hole-neck of the tube.
Balance all iodixanol gradient tubes with cell lysis buffer to make them identical in weight.
Seal the balanced tubes with black caps, ensuring no air remains inside the tube.
Centrifuge at 462,000 × g for 1 hour at 18°C using a Beckman Type 70 Ti rotor.
Carefully carry the rotor from ultracentrifugation.
Remove the tubes from the rotor with sterilized forceps.
Place the tube on the holding stand in the biosafety cabinet.
Prepare a 10 mL syringe with a 19-gauge needle.
Puncture the tube below approximately 1–2 mm of the 40%–60% interface with a 19-gauge needle with the bevel up.
Withdraw 3–4 ml of the AAV-containing 40% iodixanol layer from the bottom of the layer.
Concentrate the collected AAV fraction in pre-wet Amicon™ Ultra-15 Centrifugal Filter Units.
Centrifuge at 4,500 × g for 45 min at 4°C.
Ensure the flat surface of the filter membrane is perpendicular to the direction of fluid flow.
Discard the flow-through and add 4 mL of pre-cooled PBS to the top of the filter.
Centrifuge at 4,500 × g for 45 min at 4°C.
Repeat steps until AAV solution becomes clear and volume is approximately 50–100 μL.
Collect the AAV solution from the filter and transfer it to a 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 13,000 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant containing AAV particles (approximately 45–95 μL) to a 1.5 mL tube.
Aliquot the AAV solution into 10 μL and store it at -80°C.
Take 2 μL of AAV solution for titration.
Prepare a standard curve with AAV plasmid containing the WPRE element.
Make six serial dilutions of standard plasmid from 1 × 10^11 to 1 × 10^6 copies/mL through 10-fold dilution.
Dilute the AAV solution by adding 2 μL of AAV solution to 198 μL of PBS.
Add 2 μL of each diluted AAV solution and standard plasmid into 50 μL of PCR alkaline digestion buffer.
Denature AAV samples and standard plasmid at 100°C for 10 min.
Add 50 μL of neutralization buffer and mix by vortexing.
Perform real-time qPCR using the IQ5 Real-Time PCR machine (Bio-Rad).
Analyze data using iQ5 optical system software.
Determine the titration of AAV samples as viral genome copies per mL.
Multiply the titration of the AAV stock by 100 because the AAV sample is diluted to a 1:100 ratio.
Sterilize surgical tools and supplies, including forceps, fine scissors, and cotton swabs, using an autoclave.
Disinfect the surgical area with sporicidal disinfectant.
Equip the surgery area with a stereotaxic frame.
Connect an isoflurane vaporizer to the mouse gas anesthesia head holder.
Attach a vacuum tubing to the mouse gas anesthesia head holder for air suction.
Place a high-speed stereotaxic drill beside the stereotaxic instrument.
Position a microinjector beside the stereotaxic instrument.
Turn on the heating pad and set it to around 37°C.
Prepare borosilicate glass capillary tubes for viral injections using a micropipette puller.
Induce anesthesia in the mouse using isoflurane gas at 2% concentration.
Place the anesthetized mouse in a sealed induction chamber for approximately 1-2 minutes.
Take out the anesthetized mouse from the chamber.
Shave the hair of the mouse head using an electric hair clipper/trimmer.
Place the mouse back in the anesthesia induction chamber when it awakens during shaving.
Fix the head in the stereotaxic frame with two ear bars and a nose clamp equipped with a gas anesthesia head holder.
Supply 2% isoflurane gas to the anesthesia head holder.
Monitor the reflex from the toe-pinch to ensure deep anesthesia.
Reduce the isoflurane gas to 1% if the reflex is absent.
Monitor the depth of anesthesia periodically by performing toe-pinches during surgery.
Fix the mouse head horizontally to the base plate and vertically to the ear bars without any medial-to-lateral or front-back movements.
Apply eye lubricant to protect eyes from drying.
Wipe the mouse head with 70% ethanol.
Disinfect the scalp with 10% povidone-iodine.
Make a scalp incision using a fine scissor.
Apply 2–3 drops of 0.5% bupivacaine topically on the incision area.
Clean the exposed skull with cotton swabs dipped in sterilized PBS.
Wipe the cleaned skull with dry cotton swabs to ensure that bregma and lambda are clearly visible.
Adjust the inclination of the mouse head so that the bregma and lambda are on the same horizontal plane.
Set the coordinates of the bregma as the origin of coordinates.
Position the tip of the burr above the left PFC with AP: +2.5 mm; ML: +0.8 mm.
Lower the tip of the burr slowly until it reaches the skull surface.
Drill through the skull bone slowly under a surgical microscope until the dura mater is visible.
Puncture the dura mater if not already done, using a 30G needle tip carefully.
Stop bleeding by pressing the hole with a small cotton swab dipped in sterilized cold PBS if necessary.
Clean bony powder and excess blood from the area.
Cover the hole with sterilized PBS-soaked cotton to keep the brain surface moist before viral injection.
Drill holes in the skull at right PFC coordinates [AP: +2.5 mm, ML: ±0.8 mm].
Drill holes in the skull at bilateral BLA coordinates [AP: -1.8 mm, ML: ±3.3 mm].
Connect a Nanoject II microinjector to a stereotaxic manipulator.
Cut the tip of the glass micropipette with fine scissors to obtain a long and sharp tip.
Fill the glass micropipette with mineral oil using a 28-gauge microfil flexible needle.
Remove any air bubbles in the glass micropipette when filling it with mineral oil.
Mount a filled glass micropipette into the microinjector.
Thaw the AAV solutions on ice.
Avoid multiple freeze-thaw cycles of AAV to prevent a decrease in transduction efficiency.
Store remaining AAV at 4°C if reuse within a week is planned.
Dispose of materials contaminated with AAV in waste bottle containing 10% bleach.
Place parafilm (∼ 1 cm2) onto the mouse head in the stereotaxic frame.
Transfer a drop (1–2 μl) of AAV8-CreN-InteinN virus solution onto the parafilm.
Use a new glass micropipette for each virus.
Position the tip of the glass micropipette within the droplet of AAV8-CreN-InteinN under a surgical microscope.
Load the AAV8-CreN-InteinN slowly using the Nanoject II Fill button.
Avoid forming air bubbles in the glass micropipette.
Discard parafilm into the waste bottle containing 10% bleach solution.
Remove PBS-soaked cotton covering the left drilled hole.
Position the glass micropipette above the left PFC (AP: +2.5 mm; ML: +0.8 mm).
Lower the tip of the glass micropipette slowly to set the surface as a DV reference point.
Penetrate the brain by lowering the pipette tip until it reaches -1.5 mm from the surface.
Leave the glass micropipette in place for at least 10 minutes before injection.
Inject 300 nl of AAV8-CreN-InteinN into the PFC at a flow rate of 15–20 nl/min.
Slowly rotate the DV modulator until the tip reaches -0.5 mm from the brain surface.
Place the glass micropipette in the end position (DV: -0.5 mm) for an additional 5 minutes after injection to allow viral diffusion and prevent backflow of the virus.
Retract the glass micropipette slowly until the tip completely leaves the skull.
Move the pipette tip above the right PFC with coordinates AP: +2.5 mm, ML: -0.8 mm by rotating the AP and ML modulators.
Inject 300 nl of AAV8-CreN-InteinN into the right PFC.
Replace mineral oil-filled glass micropipette and load with AAV-retro-InteinC-CreC for injection into BLA.
Move glass micropipette above drilled hole of BLA (AP: -1.8 mm; ML: ±3.3 mm).
Lower tip slowly until close to brain surface.
Penetrate the brain by lowering tip to -4.3 mm depth from brain surface.
Inject 200 nl of AAV-retro-InteinC-CreC into each BLA (AP: -1.8 mm; ML: ±3.3 mm).
Close wound with medical-grade surgical suture.
Apply povidone-iodine to suture site to prevent possible infection in the surgical wound.
Return mouse to home cage on heating pad until it awakens and recovers from anesthesia.
Monitor health status of mouse and administer carprofen at a dose of 5 mg/kg via IP after surgery.
Allow virus to express and reconstitute split-Cre in PFC-BLA neural circuit for at least 2 weeks.
Deeply anesthetize the mouse with isoflurane in an anesthesia induction chamber.
Place the mouse on a perfusion plate and open the thoracic cavity to expose the heart using fine scissors.
Insert the 25 gauge blunt needle into the left ventricle and make a small incision in the right atrium using fine scissors.
Perfuse 50–100 mL of ice-cold PBS containing 25 U/mL heparin (5 mL/min flow rate) using a peristaltic pump.
Perfuse 50–100 mL of ice-cold 4% PFA (5 mL/min flow rate).
Extract the brain and immerse it in 4% PFA at 4°C overnight (16–24 h).
Replace 4% PFA with 30% sucrose in PBS and allow the brain to equilibrate completely at 4°C for 2 days.
Place the brain tissue on the petri dish and cut the brain into the right and left hemispheres along the midline.
Trim off the brain stem region so that the hemisphere lies flat.
Place a drop of OCT compound on the chilled cryostat chuck.
Mount the brain hemisphere on the chuck with the olfactory bulb facing upward.
Pour OCT compound on top of the brain hemisphere and return the cryostat chuck to the cryostat.
Allow the brain hemisphere to freeze in the cryostat for at least 30 minutes.
Install the chuck with the frozen brain hemisphere into the chuck holder and tighten the screw.
Cut the brain hemisphere into 50 μm coronal sections using the cryostat.
Collect sections of the PFC and BLA regions.
Place the sections containing the PFC and BLA regions into a 12 well plate with 2 mL of 0.2% TritonX-100 in PBS per well.
Incubate the sections on an orbital shaker for 15 minutes at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Stain nuclei of the sections with 1 μg/mL DAPI in 2 mL of 0.2% TritonX-100 in PBS for 15 minutes at room temperature (20°C–22°C) while shaking.
Wash the sections three times with 2 mL of 0.2% TritonX-100 in PBS for 5 minutes each.
Place the washed sections on a slide glass.
Coverslip the sections with Prolong™ glass antifade mountant.
Take images of the sections by tile scan imaging function using a confocal microscope (LSM 710) under the control of Zen software (Zeiss).
